title: EME, scatter and wave basics
blurb: Explain EME, meteor and auroral scatter, microwave ducts, and how electromagnetic waves are built.

E3A01.why: Both stations only need the Moon in view, which puts them up to about **12,000 miles** apart.
E3A01.trap: Perigee changes loss, not how far apart you can be.

E3A02.why: Libration, the Moon's rocking, keeps changing the echo path, giving a **fluttery, irregular fade**.

E3A03.why: Path loss grows with distance, so the **Moon at perigee**, its closest point, gives the least.
E3A03.trap: Moon phase and MUF don't set the path loss.

E3A04.why: E, H and the direction of travel are all mutually perpendicular: the wave travels at a **right angle to both fields**.

E3A05.why: The electric and magnetic fields sit at **right angles** to each other.
E3A05.trap: Out of phase is about timing. They are in phase, and perpendicular in space.

E3A06.why: A lower MUF means higher bands fail. Move down: a **lower-frequency band** stays below the MUF.

E3A07.why: Microwave ducts form in layered air over **large bodies of water**.

E3A08.why: Meteors burn up at E-region heights, leaving a linear ionized trail in the **E region**.

E3A09.why: Meteor trails reflect VHF well: **28 MHz to 148 MHz**.
E3A09.trap: Echoes weaken and shorten as frequency rises, so UHF is poor. HF below 28 MHz isn't used.

E3A10.why: Speed in a medium is c ÷ **index of refraction**. Higher index, slower wave.

E3A11.why: Tropospheric ducts typically carry microwaves **100 to 300 miles**.

E3A12.why: A **severe geomagnetic storm** expands the aurora to lower latitudes where it scatters signals.
E3A12.trap: Quiet conditions and meteor showers don't light up the aurora.

E3A13.why: Aurora distorts and smears signals. Narrow, simple **CW** gets through best.

E3A14.why: In circular polarization the electric and magnetic fields **rotate** as the wave travels.
E3A14.trap: Loop antennas and orbiting waves are not what makes polarization circular.
